segments.text: The Nova X5 costs twenty-four thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine rupees, and everyone is
asking whether it is worth it.
I have used it as my main phone for two weeks, and stay till
the end, because I will compare its camera directly with the Pixel.
Let us go through the screen, the performance, the battery, and whether you should
actually buy it.
The screen is bright and smooth, and videos look genuinely good on it, even
in daylight outdoors.
Scrolling feels fast, colours look rich without going over the top, and I had
no complaints watching matches on it.
On paper it is an LTPO AMOLED with high-frequency PWM dimming, UFS 3.1 storage,
a vapour chamber, and top-binned SoC silicon.
The touch sampling, the DC-like dimming curve and the panel lottery all check out,
so enthusiasts can buy with confidence.
In daily use, apps open quickly, the phone stays cool in normal tasks, and
games run smoothly at medium settings.
I played for about an hour at a stretch and the frame rate stayed
steady, which is what matters at this price.
It heated up a little during charging, which is normal for fast charging, and
cooled down right after.
The battery is the best part: it easily lasts three days of heavy use,
gaming, video and hotspot included.
I never once reached for a charger during the day, and you probably will
not need to either.
The cameras are decent in daylight: sharp photos, pleasant colours, and a night mode
that does a fair job.
Portraits look clean, the ultrawide is usable in good light, and selfies are better
than I expected.
At just two hundred and ninety-nine dollars, it undercuts everything on Verizon and T-Mobile
right now.
Walk into any Best Buy and you will see phones costing twice as much
doing half as well.
It gets two years of software updates, which is standard at this price, so
factor that into your decision.
If you keep phones for three or four years, think about whether that update
window is enough for you.
Now, if you cannot afford a real flagship, I guess this is fine for
you people, it takes photos and makes calls.
Some of you will never appreciate a proper premium phone anyway, so just buy
this and stop complaining.
The fingerprint sensor is fast, face unlock works in the dark, and the speakers
are loud enough for videos.
Call quality was clear on both ends, and the vibration motor feels nicer than
last year's model.
One tip: just leave it charging under your pillow overnight, it gets a little
warm but that warmth is totally normal.
Keep it tucked under there every night and you will always wake up to
a full battery, no problem at all.
So, should you buy it?
If your budget is around twenty-five thousand rupees, this is one of the strongest
options.
Compare it with two rivals on exchange offers and bank discounts before you decide,
prices move every week.
That is my full review.
